corrections: 1. The Associations and Foundations Law (Biedribu un nodibinajumu likums) was adopted 30 Oct 2003 and in force 1 Apr 2004, not 2014/2015; there is no '2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law' - remove that claim. 2. Last published official state fee for registering an association/foundation was EUR 11.38 (Cabinet Reg. No. 308), with a 10% reduction for e-filing via registrs.ur.gov.lv; ~$33 looks too high (approx. $12-13). 3. Notes are self-contradictory (notary step vs no notary); e-filing with a Latvian/EU e-signature needs no notary.

1. 'NVO' is not a legal form; the Lithuanian forms are association (asociacija, Law on Associations), public institution (viesoji istaiga) and charity and support foundation (labdaros ir paramos fondas).

1. Cite the governing laws: Ley Organica 1/2002 (associations) and Ley 50/2002 (state foundations) plus regional foundation laws; EUR 30,000 endowment applies to foundations. 2. An asociacion registered under LO 1/2002 is not 'unincorporated' (it has legal personality from its founding act); 'SL/SA charitable societies' are not a charitable entity type.

1. Private foundations require recognition under the Lei-Quadro das Fundacoes (Lei 24/2012, as amended); patrimonial sufficiency is presumed only above the threshold fixed by Portaria 75/2013 (reported as EUR 250,000 for national-scope foundations, with a cash portion), so 'no statutory minimum endowment' is misleading. 2. Recognition is granted by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers; 'Instituto' is not a separate private charitable legal form.

1. Minimum patrimony for legal personality via RUNTS under art. 22 Codice del Terzo Settore (D.Lgs. 117/2017) is EUR 30,000 for foundations (EUR 15,000 for associations), attested by the notary - not EUR 150,000; update fee/notes accordingly.

1. The Amutot Law 5740-1980 requires only two or more founders (not 7 or '2-3'); seven members is a common practical/bylaw convention after registration. 2. The entity is an 'amuta' registered with the Registrar of Amutot (Israeli Corporations Authority).

1. Governing law is the Law on Societies No. 51 of 2008 (amended by Law No. 22 of 2009); registration is with the National Registry of Societies at the Ministry of Social Development (not 'Ministry of Social Affairs'). 2. Minimum 7 founders (except closed societies), founders must be Jordanian nationals 18+; foreign funding requires Council of Ministers approval.

1. Governing law is the Ottoman Law of Associations of 3 Aug 1909, applied via notification (ilm wa khabar) to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities (see Circular 10/AM/2006); associations controlled by foreigners may be treated as foreign associations subject to separate authorization, so 'no nationality rule' should be softened.

1. No new associations law has been enacted: registration is still governed by Law No. 93 of 1958 on Associations and Private Institutions (amended by Legislative Decree 224/1969); a replacement draft by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor was still unpublished as of Sept 2026. 2. MoSAL's 1 Oct 2025 directive enforces prior approval for foreign affiliations/funding (Arts. 21, 66, 69).

1. Registration is with the NGOs Department of the Secretariat General of the Council of Ministers, not the Interior Ministry. 2. Law 12/2010 has no 10-founder minimum; the application must be signed by at least 3 founders who are Iraqi nationals or residents of Iraq (foreigners need a valid residence card). 3. Kurdistan Region NGOs register separately under KRG Law 1/2011.

1. There is no '2024 Civil Society Law (Royal Decree M/111)'; the governing law is the Law of Associations and Foundations (Royal Decree M/8, 1437H), approved by Cabinet 1 Dec 2015, in force 17 Mar 2016, with implementing regulations of Apr 2016, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development / National Center for Non-Profit Sector Development. 2. 10 Saudi founders minimum and ban on foreign branches confirmed under that law.

1. Cite the specific instruments: Law 24/1962 on Clubs and Public Welfare Societies (min. 10 founders, all Kuwaiti, age 21+), and the 2025 MoSA charity regulation (Ministerial Decision No. 90) cutting charitable-association founders from 50 to 10 Kuwaitis. 2. Decree-Law No. 87 of 2026 created the National Center for Charitable and Humanitarian Work to regulate charitable activity - add this. Foreign formation remains closed.

1. There is no '2023 philanthropy law' (the cited 2023 item is an ICNL report). The governing law is Decree-Law No. 21 of 2020 on Private Associations and Institutions (replacing Law 12/2004), with charitable activity regulated by Law No. 15 of 2014 and the Regulatory Authority for Charitable Activities (RACA).

1. Federal Law 2/2008 was repealed (not amended) by Federal Decree-Law No. 50 of 2023 on Non-Profit Organisations (public benefit associations, civil society foundations, etc.); the 70% UAE-national founder rule comes from the repealed 2008 law and should be re-checked against FDL 50/2023 and its executive regulations. 2. Dubai entities are additionally governed by Dubai Law No. 12 of 2017.

1. Royal Decree 64/2026 (8 Jun 2026, Official Gazette 1652, in force 15 Jun 2026) promulgated the Civil Society Institutions Law and repealed the Civil Associations Law (RD 14/2000, as amended by RD 23/2007 which required 40+ founders); existing bodies have one year to regularize and executive regulations are due within a year.
